::: {.hero-eyebrow}
Boğaziçi University
:::
# Computational Social Science Society {.hero-title}
::: {.hero-lede}
We are students and researchers at Boğaziçi University who study social questions
with computational methods. We meet weekly for hands-on sessions, and we build
things together — models, datasets, and small simulations anyone can run.
:::
:::
:::

::: {.content-body}

::: {.prose}
::: {.eyebrow}
What we do
:::

## Social questions, computational instruments

The society brings together people from political science, sociology, economics,
history, and computer engineering. Our shared premise is that many social questions
turn on processes we cannot observe directly — how opinions spread, how ties form,
how what people say diverges from what they believe. Computational methods let us
state those processes precisely and test them against data.

Sessions are informal and hands-on. Someone brings a problem or a paper, we work
through the code together, and everyone leaves with something they can run. No
prior programming experience is required to attend — several of our current members
started with none.
:::

::: {.eyebrow}
Methods
:::

::: {.methods}

::: {.method}
### Agent-based modeling
Building populations of interacting agents to see which macro patterns follow from
which micro rules. We work mainly in NetLogo and Python.
:::

::: {.method}
### Network analysis
Treating relationships as data: alliance networks, retweet networks, co-authorship.
Descriptive statistics through to ERGMs and community detection.
:::

::: {.method}
### Text as data
Turning documents, speeches, and social media into measurable quantities, with
particular attention to Turkish-language NLP.
:::

::: {.method}
### Machine learning
Prediction and classification applied to social data, alongside the harder question
of when prediction is and is not the right tool.
:::

:::

::: {.prose}
::: {.eyebrow}
Joining
:::

## Come to a session

We meet weekly during term at the Department of Political Science and International
Relations. Meetings are open — no membership form, no prerequisite. Bring a laptop
if you have one.

Write to us at the address on the [contact page](contact.qmd) and we will add you to
the mailing list for meeting times and readings.
:::

:::
